doc.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

chapter: Metronome All Stars and Charlie Parker
title: Metronome All Stars and the call from Charlie Parker
summary: He describes Parker, Miles and Dizzy in the All Stars, and wishing aloud for Bird to call him; Bird phoned within weeks.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: But you, from ‘47 to ‘43 you played with the Metronome All Stars, is that right?
‘47 to ‘53. I’m sorry. It’s still early in the morning you know.
Yes. I’ve been watching the time.
I’ve got to go to a wedding. I’ll put my tie on. I’m sorry I don’t put a tie on.
No, you’re fine, believe me. In the Metronome All Stars with Diz and Miles and Charlie Parker.

Well Charlie was sort of nice to me. Miles was funny with me. Dizzy was all right. I mean he talked to me. And Charlie was very good too. I mean if we were walking, I’d be in another place, across the street on 52nd Street, and he used to walk around with this horn and just sit in every night. He’d walk around with her in the summertime. He’d walk in and play a couple of choruses and walk out and go to the next. place Well heard me playing all the time you know, so I was very surprised, I don’t know, like I said this before, but when me and Serge was coming home from one of them All Star dates, and we were in the car, and talking, just talking like this. And Serge said something like, “Do you realize we were on the All Star tape, like the biggest thing in the country, like Dizzy © Fillius Jazz Archive -22-

and Charlie” blah blah blah. So I says, “Yeah well that’s because you know like we just happened to do.” He says, “Well what would make you happier than that?” I says, “If Charlie called me up for his record date.” And within a couple of weeks I’m sitting there, “Oh, BB?” I says, “Yeah?” “This is the Bird.” See so.
That’s right. I didn’t do so good but he did it.

Well I mean it’s satisfying. So no matter what anybody says to me you know, you’re not so good, blah, blah, blah. I said well you do it then. You know like a lot of my, especially guitar players, and they can play better than me really, you know like we sit down — so they said how did you get so big? I says I don’t know. I said the phone rang.

Yeah, so they keep on saying. I says well why don’t you do it? I can’t help it. You know what I mean? And they are good, but maybe it’s this other quality, that I can get along with these people. Just like we’re sitting here talking, you don’t feel any strain to make me talk, do you?
Can I have all the outtakes? How long is that?
We can wrap up pretty soon here, because I know you have to get going. Here’s a hard question maybe. How’s that for an introduction?
